**The SC Legislature passed a budget. Communities lost the most with no earmarks.**
South Carolina state government has been operating under a continuing resolution since July 1 because the legislature was unable to finalize a spending plan before the start of the new fiscal year.
Budget writers set aside $377.7 million for lawmaker projects in a separate piece of legislation. They gave themselves a Sept. 30 deadline to allocate the money, but lawmakers would have had to come back in the fall to approve a supplemental spending bill, which risks the possibility of negative headlines on certain projects less than two months before the November election.
Budget negotiators had agreed to have a joint committee decide how much money each earmark received. That went out the window as budget writers tried to resolve earmark funding before Tuesday’s session, and communities are the ones who will lose the most.[ Read more here.](https://us.list-manage.com/16ZLXxGO9x7?e=edbde6c9b1&c2id=d580cd1bdfbc15e62e8fc86070aa989a)

## Trump Ready to Spend Super PAC Cash
President Trump on Friday announced that he is prepared to [_spend "a lot" of money_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO5CAQBNCvwZlHTIMxDggucTaXXmgxprH7BMaC3hnt36-80n7BxiVV6dW_x_LwlOjY_vqMjmNZDny3hMxYl-w3f_qVfd2QW6bAWHNr2S8gwfTS9qAWvzK9cNG-Cy4iAqoO3X20ox6nYRq63Q3meZdDeKqnHQeU0WiAySgPCm1QMXbkrj5pQd2lNErdNADEqO1qIWCYJqElBuJSb_8LHbxjTJ_lhfW2ltwltzOfTag_AmYBM--4U0pXJmDeS8aLJGD2IdNBjatnKoeA2UitDdie60c--3biEejY-ovdn37tf8QC5q66cL4pJWpmFFpu2dP3RMe_fO3l4CsAAP__OFKClw) from his MAGA Inc. super PAC to support GOP candidates ahead of the November midterm elections. Trump said, _" I will tell you it's about $850 million. I'll be spending a lot of that money for--and my own money--but I'll be spending a lot of that money for candidates that I think are good, Republican candidates."_ The super PAC did not spend on any candidates [_in June or July_](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGO4yAQgOGnMR3WZCC2KSiucZdrr7QIjG1OYCyYjZW3X2VfYetf-or_32N5uJjisf11mSyvZTnoaomYqS7Zbe50nl3diFuOganm1rJbEHCQMElUi_McX7RoJ4JdiZCUIHsbp1GP5m7uYrfeDD7ALdDwfAYDBHdc6ekHoyckZVBE-_FgQnUDGJTqNSKuq578hIGCMZ0GCpFL7f-XePBOa3qXF9XelyyS3ZnP1qk_Hc4dztd19a6kT-twdpWjT9Q6nLl-5VM2924yJdlOOoJMhSWi1mAAoN85J1FtOK-YUmzD2GnYsos_mOBf_nlZ_A4AAP__pK16lA), but Trump said the money would be sent "very soon." Also on Friday, White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said she will [return to work for MAGA, Inc.](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2u3CAQRp8Gd6zYMf4rKLax0ty0Ka0RDDa5YCwYL8rbR5tXSP1Jn845v762LwwxnPtPTGTY5-2kViMxU9kS7nihZSw7cU3BMZVUa8INFIxSzRL6DS2HN20aO2c8EVDfkXlO86SnZViG7jBu0BpxosEqhPE5L8951BZw7PU4gKUumM-fmqF_KjX2_UMDgPd6tjM4cssitCIXOJfH7xxOPsjHP_lN5WFz6qI5mK8q-peAVcDaWnuken42ASud8q4C1o-WgDXzQUXAGgnfgVlyli2Xb4ksudzpkuh9iAGZnKz3RUVeaKXPMeYWzl22IzDJI9-VpKMLC9-FBKxY5OsF-IOG764Yd7UQY6jjJLTaE4b4j5T_M_DbwN8AAAD__76bkq0), where she served as a spokesperson before joining Trump's 2024 campaign. **Whatever happened to TV Infomercials?** If you ever found yourself wide awake at 2 a.m., mesmerized by a man slicing tomatoes paper-thin while shouting "_But wait, there's more!_ " then you already know about the golden age of TV infomercials. And odds are, [the man doing the slicing was Ron Popeil](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOqzAQheGnMV2QGUMwhYtIN6luttliSzTYY_DKhshMjPL2q-wrbHuO9BX_1328Y4hhnT8wkWG_jSsdeyRmymPCGR9oGfNMvKfgmHLa94QjSDifpD6BGtFyKDS2WDnjiYBURabpdd_2Qzd01WKcJ9tMU-d6rydlJ-lJIigYet1MrqMqmLcnNahGyrNSdQsA3rfaanDkhkG0klzgLdffW1h5IR9fW6Fc2y1V0SzMj12oi4CbgNtxHPVre_Jzovf_XpDtItStCPVvhc_rJf-_ljJX2bjHEWIM-7kXrZwThvhL8h9LFAM_AQAA__8M3XPK). Popeil essentially invented the format. He started hawking kitchen gadgets at 16 on Chicago's Maxwell Street, then took his pitch to television in 1959 [with the Chop-O-Matic](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGngS3oOBNsDx6qtnRK14yWwWdwZccRXEB5-yp9ha7fJ_2G__ViLy6meJu_XSbDodgbHVsiZlptdrO7u4ndOhNvOXqmNW9bdhYB-xOoEwrrJo472c7V3gQiJFGTaaWSndRnfa4XIzWADwCjVmf0EASOUgC26En1rW7raF4eKBQtQC9E0yFiCJ2aFHryWlcdkI9c1uanxBsvFNKz7LQ2U8l1MgvzfavEW4VDhcNxHM2zPPgx0ut_LY6npRLDXomP4avIq83j9f2zXo2_HzGluPWy6mDOLqY_kv9ZYjf4GwAA__9qTnHd)**.** His company, Ronco, became a household name, and when the FCC relaxed its rules on program-length commercials in 1984, the floodgates opened. Suddenly, every insomniac in America was a captive audience for the Veg-O-Matic, [the Pocket Fisherman](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFugzAQxvGnMVuQOTuABw-Vqmzpmm7oyp3BqR1SfAHl7av0Fbp-n_Qb_pfzcMaY4m36wMxewjLceC-JRXgdMk54x1FwnVhKjiS85lIyDqChPej-AGbAUeLGg8WKfGAGNhX7pus727mjO1azb4_WMgUiR2iJddM7bBxpMJ1tCHUV_cvTPZhG69aY2gJACLYfeyAm55TVTFGWtb4u8SYzh_RcNl7rcclV8rPIvSjzpuCk4LTve_1cHvL44tf_WlDGWZnTpsz743oxP8GF5-d3tXq67zGlWNpOWT1ljOmPlH-W2Dz8BgAA__99W3NX), the Flowbee, and Popeil's masterpiece--the Showtime Rotisserie, which moved over a billion dollars in sales on the strength of four unforgettable words: "_Set it and forget it_." Other pitchmen followed. Billy Mays brought his thundering "_Hi, Billy Mays here!_ " to OxiClean. Kevin Trudeau sold millions of diet books before a federal judge sent him to prison for fraud. The format became so iconic that SNL parodied it repeatedly, starting with [Dan Aykroyd's legendary Bass-O-Matic sketch](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LFurDAQheGnMd0iMzbYFC6udEW3SZkSzZqxcWQvCGZB-_YReYW050hf8X_dxzumnJ7xAws5Dsv4pHPPxEzbWDDiip5xi8R7SRPTVva94AgSupu0N1Ajek4HjRqryQUiIFWRa4w12vRt31azC9qHvgFvje1aUmh8E3qNpm1lQNmoKrnLkxZUI2WnVK0BIARtvYWJpr4XWtKUeNnq7yU9eaaQ38tBW-2XUmU3M6-7UP8EDAKG8zzr9_Li14Ou_1qQ_SzUcAj1P65xTXh-Do9YbW5az5Rz2jsjtIwFU_4l-Y8lDgc_AQAA__9FNXM1) in 1976. Then the audience vanished. Streaming killed the graveyard slot. Mays died in 2009 at 50. Popeil followed in 2021 at 86. Ronco filed for bankruptcy and was liquidated in 2018. But the infomercial didn't really die--it just moved. Today's version is TikTok Shop, where energetic creators demo products live with a buy button baked right in. The platform is projected to top $20 billion in U.S. sales this year, and one creator with fewer than 40,000 followers pulled in nearly $2 million in a single month. The TikTok Shop DNA is pure Popeil: charismatic personality, live demo, manufactured urgency, impulse buy. He just would've needed a shorter pitch. _Did you ever buy a Ronco product?
